newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: SWEDEN AGREES TO CANCEL SOME MOZAMBICAN DEBT.
newsitem.headline: SWEDEN AGREES TO CANCEL SOME MOZAMBICAN DEBT.

text.p: Sweden has agreed to cancel two-thirds of the debt service owed by Mozambique for the period 1995-1999, Swedish ambassador Helena Odmark said on Tuesday.
The amount of debt forgiven amounts to US$4.1 million.
The remaining two million dollars has been resceduled over 23 years.
"The debt involves long-term trade credits extended in the 1980's by the Swedish state," Odmark told Reuters.
This debt relief is in line with a decision by the Paris Club of creditors last November, which agreed to grant Mozambique "Naples terms".
Under these terms, 67 percent of debt servicing due over a given period is scrapped, while the rest is rescheduled over at least 20 years.
